story: The federal AI money with an Alaska name on it is an 8(a) services contract, and FPDS phrase search can't reliably find it

claims.claim: An FPDS phrase search for Alaska vendors and the phrase artificial intelligence returns 24 contract actions.
claims.verbatim: DELIVERY ORDER W911QX20F0088 (P00014) awarded to STAMPEDE VENTURES, INC, was modified for the amount of $25,031.45
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: Counted by the fact-checker today. The feed emits no opensearch totalResults element and ignores feedmax, so paged start=0,5,10,15,20 then 25. The quoted entry is the 24th and final record; start=25 returned zero entries.

claims.claim: An FPDS phrase search for Alaska vendors and the longer phrase artificial intelligence, and machine learning returns 25 contract actions.
claims.verbatim: DEFINITIVE CONTRACT HQ003425CE092 (P00007) awarded to LEISNOI PROFESSIONAL SERVICES, LLC, was modified for the amount of $3,184,887.72
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: Paged start=0,5,10,15,20,25 today, confirmed by a zero entry read past the end. Counted as feed records: the ATOM feed emits one entry per contract action, so the 25 actions are the 25 records the query returns, which is the word the slide uses.

claims.claim: The longer phrase is a strict superset of the shorter one, yet none of the 25 records it returns appear among the 24 returned by the shorter phrase.
claims.verbatim: New DEFINITIVE CONTRACT HQ003425CE092 awarded to LEISNOI PROFESSIONAL SERVICES, LLC for $8,728,231.32
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: THE DECK'S CENTRAL CLAIM, reproduced from scratch. The 24 short-query records are five actions on 140D0421C0002, three on FA489026C0006, three on FA701426C0017, one on W519TC26CA019 and twelve on W911QX20F0088. The 25 long-query records are fourteen on 140D0419C0047, three on HQ003425CE012 and eight on HQ003425CE092. The two sets are completely disjoint.

claims.claim: A search for Alaska artificial intelligence contracts misses three contracts worth $54,250,832.04 that a longer phrase containing the same words does return.
claims.verbatim: New DEFINITIVE CONTRACT HQ003425CE012 awarded to KONIAG IT SYSTEMS, LLC for $4,600,000
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: Sum of the three hidden contracts, each totalled from FPDS actions read today. 140D0419C0047 at $21,596,322.25 plus HQ003425CE012 at $12,022,390.38 plus HQ003425CE092 at $20,632,119.41. The latter two were each confirmed independently against usaspending.

claims.claim: The Leisnoi contract description that the shorter search misses reads information technology, artificial intelligence, and machine learning program support services.
claims.verbatim: THIS IS A NON-PERSONAL SERVICES CONTRACT TO PROVIDE INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AND MACHINE LEARNING PROGRAM SUPPORT SERVICES.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: Exact base award text. Later modifications drop the opening clause.

claims.claim: In every record the two searches returned, a description is missed by the shorter phrase when a comma immediately follows the words artificial intelligence and found when a parenthesis or another word follows.
claims.verbatim: IT, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI), AND MACHINE LEARNING (ML) PROGRAMMATIC SUPPORT SERVICES FOR THE DOD CHIEF INFORMATION OFFICER (DOD CIO) JOINT AI CENTER (JAIC)
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: SOFTEN ON THE SLIDE. Pattern holds across all 49 descriptions read, and the quoted record is the sharpest test because it contains a comma placed after (AI) rather than after INTELLIGENCE, and it IS returned. This is a hypothesis consistent with the data, not a proven mechanism. C03 is the publishable finding and does not depend on this.

claims.claim: Leisnoi Professional Services LLC holds a Washington Headquarters Services contract obligated at $20,632,119.41.
claims.verbatim: LEISNOI PROFESSIONAL SERVICES, LLC
claims.source_outlet: USAspending.gov award record
claims.notes: The eight FPDS actions were summed independently to exactly the same figure, so two federal systems agree to the cent.

claims.claim: The Leisnoi contract has obligated its entire ceiling with nothing left unspent.
claims.verbatim: LEISNOI PROFESSIONAL SERVICES, LLC
claims.source_outlet: USAspending.gov award record
claims.notes: Total obligation, base and all options value, and base exercised options value all reported identical. A ceiling fully obligated at the end of a period of performance is normal and is not by itself evidence of anything irregular.

claims.claim: The Leisnoi contract reached its total across 8 separate contract actions.
claims.verbatim: DEFINITIVE CONTRACT HQ003425CE092 (P00007) awarded to LEISNOI PROFESSIONAL SERVICES, LLC, was modified for the amount of $3,184,887.72
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: Base award plus P00001 through P00007. P00003 is negative at minus $40,969.05.

claims.claim: The Leisnoi contract was awarded as an 8(a) sole source under NAICS code 541512 for computer systems design services.
claims.verbatim: 8(A) SOLE SOURCE
claims.source_outlet: USAspending.gov award record
claims.notes: NAICS 541512 COMPUTER SYSTEMS DESIGN SERVICES, product service code R499. An AI contract classified and bought as professional services.

claims.claim: The Leisnoi contract runs from September 11th, 2025 to September 10th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: LEISNOI PROFESSIONAL SERVICES, LLC
claims.source_outlet: USAspending.gov award record
claims.notes: Start 2025-09-11, current end and potential end both 2026-09-10. The contract expires two days after this run date.

claims.claim: The Leisnoi artificial intelligence contract is performed in Washington DC and not in Alaska.
claims.verbatim: WASHINGTON, DC 20301
claims.source_outlet: USAspending.gov award record
claims.notes: Vendor address 101 W Benson Blvd Ste 202, Anchorage, AK 99503, but the work is performed at the Pentagon ZIP. The honest shape of the story.

claims.claim: Koniag Emerging Technologies LLC holds an Army contract worth $5,267,244.80 for artificial intelligence rapid support.
claims.verbatim: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) RAPID SUPPORT (AIRS) IN SUPPORT OF DEPUTY TO THE CHIEF DIGITAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE OFFICE (CDAO) ENTERPRISE PROGRAMS
claims.source_outlet: USAspending.gov award record
claims.notes: PIID W519TC26CA019, confirmed independently in FPDS at the same amount. Awarding office W6QK ACC-RI, Department of the Army.

claims.claim: The Koniag Emerging Technologies artificial intelligence contract is performed in Anchorage.
claims.verbatim: 8(A) SOLE SOURCE
claims.source_outlet: USAspending.gov award record
claims.notes: Place of performance Anchorage, Alaska 99503. NAICS 518210, computing infrastructure providers and data processing.

claims.claim: The Koniag Emerging Technologies contract was signed on May 29th, 2026 and can run to May 25th, 2031 if every option is exercised.
claims.verbatim: KONIAG EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES LLC
claims.source_outlet: USAspending.gov award record
claims.notes: Signed 2026-05-29, current end 2027-05-28, potential end 2031-05-25. Say potential end, never simply runs to 2031.

claims.claim: Exactly one federal contract record has both a place of performance in Alaska and the phrase artificial intelligence in its description.
claims.verbatim: New DEFINITIVE CONTRACT W519TC26CA019 awarded to KONIAG EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES LLC for the amount of $5,267,244.8
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: CARRY THE CAVEAT. This is what the query returns and is not a claim about the world. Given C03 and C06, any Alaska performed contract whose description places a comma after artificial intelligence would be invisible to this same query. Note also that the field name PRINCIPAL_PLACE_STATE_NAME silently returns zero records, a second way this search misleads a careful user.

claims.claim: Nine federal records have a place of performance in Alaska and the phrase machine learning, and every one of them is a NASA grant to the University of Alaska Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: INVESTIGATING THE CONTRIBUTION OF AURORAL BEAD EVENTS TO SUBSTORM ONSET A STATISTICAL STUDY USING MACHINE LEARNING AND CITIZEN SCIENCE
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: Paged start=0 for five, start=5 for four more, start=10 zero. Four distinct grant numbers, 80NSSC20K1279, 80NSSC23K0227, 80NSSC25K7296 and 80NSSC25K7546.

claims.claim: Those nine Alaska performed machine learning records total $1,187,674.80.
claims.verbatim: COMBINING SAR REMOTE SENSING AND MACHINE LEARNING TO ADVANCE FLOOD MONITORING AND LANDSLIDE HAZARD ASSESSMENT IN THE HKH
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: Summed independently to the same figure the scout reported. Two of the nine are negative deobligations. All Alaska performed machine learning research here is worth about 6 percent of the single Leisnoi services contract.

claims.claim: Tuknik Government Services holds a contract for the Defense Department Joint Artificial Intelligence Center totalling $24,210,536.43.
claims.verbatim: IT, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI), AND MACHINE LEARNING (ML) PROGRAMMATIC SUPPORT SERVICES FOR THE DOD CHIEF INFORMATION OFFICER (DOD CIO) JOINT AI CENTER (JAIC)
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: PIID 140D0421C0002, sum of five FPDS actions signed December 21st, 2020 to September 24th, 2021. This contract IS returned by the short query, unlike the other Tuknik one.

claims.claim: An earlier Tuknik contract for the same programmatic support work totals $21,596,322.25 across 14 actions.
claims.verbatim: INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AND MACHINE LEARNING PROGRAMMATIC SUPPORT SERVICES
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: PIID 140D0419C0047, base award March 22nd, 2019 through P00013 on February 15th, 2023, including one deobligation of minus $177,282.96. This CORRECTS the scout, which reported roughly $9,479,118.55 as a floor, being only the first three obligating actions.

claims.claim: Koniag IT Systems LLC held the same Washington Headquarters Services work before Leisnoi, totalling $12,022,390.38.
claims.verbatim: KONIAG IT SYSTEMS, LLC
claims.source_outlet: USAspending.gov award record
claims.notes: PIID HQ003425CE012. usaspending total matches the sum of three FPDS actions to the cent. Same NAICS 541512, same 8(a) sole source, same awarding office, identical description to the Leisnoi award.

claims.claim: The Koniag IT Systems contract ended on September 10th, 2025 and the Leisnoi contract began the next day.
claims.verbatim: 8(A) SOLE SOURCE
claims.source_outlet: USAspending.gov award record
claims.notes: HQ003425CE012 current and potential end both 2025-09-10. HQ003425CE092 start and date signed both 2025-09-11. State the dates and let the reader draw the inference. Do NOT assert coordination, which is not in evidence.

claims.claim: Tuknik Government Services is a wholly owned subsidiary of Koniag Government Services.
claims.verbatim: TGS is an Alaska Native Corporation (ANC), and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Koniag Government Services, LLC (KGS), an ANC.
claims.source_outlet: Koniag Government Services
claims.notes: The company's own statement. Settles the Kodiak chain question the scout left open.

claims.claim: Koniag Government Services lists 28 wholly owned subsidiaries, among them one named Koniag AI Solutions LLC.
claims.verbatim: KGS has a family of wholly-owned subsidiaries with diverse capabilities and offerings.
claims.source_outlet: Koniag Government Services
claims.notes: 28 names counted on the page, including Koniag AI Solutions LLC, Koniag Emerging Technologies LLC, Koniag IT Systems LLC, Koniag Services Inc and Tuknik Government Services LLC.

claims.claim: Koniag AI Solutions LLC describes itself as a process, distribution and logistics consulting company rather than an artificial intelligence developer.
claims.verbatim: Koniag AI Solutions, LLC (KAIS) is a process, distribution, and logistics consulting company that focuses on using technology for these processes.
claims.source_outlet: Koniag Government Services
claims.notes: Primary NAICS 541614, process and logistics consulting. The firm with AI in its name is classified as logistics consulting.

claims.claim: Koniag subsidiaries signed 30 federal contract actions in the two weeks ending September 7th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: KONIAG EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES LLC
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: Paged start=0,5,10,15,20,25 and confirmed start=30 returns zero entries. The federal fiscal year end wall.

claims.claim: Those 30 Koniag actions were spread across more than a dozen federal departments and agencies.
claims.verbatim: KONIAG ADVISORY AND BUSINESS SOLUTIONS, LLC
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: The fact-checker counts 13 departments where the scout said 12, and 16 at the contracting office level. Agriculture, Commerce via the Patent and Trademark Office, Labor, State, Treasury via the Bureau of Engraving and Printing, Social Security Administration, International Trade Commission, General Services Administration, National Science Foundation, Environmental Protection Agency, Homeland Security, Health and Human Services via Indian Health Service, and Energy. THE SLIDE WRITES more than a dozen, because the count is sensitive to how offices roll up.

claims.claim: A Department of Energy contract modification to Koniag Emerging Technologies states its purpose as adding an AI tool.
claims.verbatim: THE PURPOSE OF THIS MODIFICATION IS TO ADD AI TOOL
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: PIID 89303026CIM000014, modification P00002, signed June 26th, 2026, obligating $3,259,129.83. The string is exactly as quoted, no trailing period, no article before AI TOOL. This is the whole stated justification.

claims.claim: That Department of Energy contract carries a ceiling of $34,301,950.89 against $7,855,836.13 obligated so far.
claims.verbatim: KONIAG EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES LLC
claims.source_outlet: USAspending.gov award record
claims.notes: 8(a) sole source, NAICS 541990, performed in Washington DC 20585 for the Office of the Chief Information Officer. The scout's claim of a raise FROM $24,524,561.40 was killed, because usaspending publishes only the current ceiling. Do NOT print a before and after.

claims.claim: The Department of Energy added $679,233.27 to that contract on September 3rd, 2026.
claims.verbatim: KONIAG EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES LLC
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: Strong internal cross check. Six earlier actions sum to $7,176,602.86, plus this equals $7,855,836.13, exactly the usaspending total in C29.

claims.claim: Federal law requires regional Alaska Native corporations to share 70 percent of their timber and subsurface revenue with the other eleven.
claims.verbatim: 70 percent of all revenues received by each Regional Corporation from the timber resources and subsurface estate patented to it pursuant to this chapter shall be divided annually by the Regional Corporation among all twelve Regional Corporations
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Law Revision Counsel, United States Code
claims.notes: 43 U.S.C. 1606(i)(1)(A), statute text read today.

claims.claim: That sharing requirement names only timber and the subsurface estate and does not name services or government contracting revenue.
claims.verbatim: from the timber resources and subsurface estate patented to it pursuant to this chapter
claims.source_outlet: Office of the Law Revision Counsel, United States Code
claims.notes: SOFTENED. The subsection names timber and subsurface, carves out sand, gravel, stone, pumice, peat, clay and cinder, and nowhere mentions services or contracting. The correct sentence is that the sharing rule covers resource revenue and does not reach government contracting. Do NOT write that the law explicitly exempts contracting. It is silent, and the silence is the claim.

claims.claim: Koniag raised its annual dividend by three dollars to 33 dollars per share.
claims.verbatim: Kodiak's regional Native corporation is growing its shareholders, dividends & finances
claims.source_outlet: KMXT Kodiak Public Broadcasting, reported by Davis Hovey
claims.notes: Background, outside the run window, label it as such. The distribution date is given as January 27 with no year in the readable text, so print the day without the year or drop the date.

claims.claim: Koniag pays an elder benefit of 1,200 dollars to original shareholders aged 62 and over.
claims.verbatim: Kodiak's regional Native corporation is growing its shareholders, dividends & finances
claims.source_outlet: KMXT Kodiak Public Broadcasting, reported by Davis Hovey
claims.notes: Background, outside the window. Attribute to KMXT on the slide.

claims.claim: Koniag has grown from 3,400 shareholders at incorporation to more than 4,700 today.
claims.verbatim: Kodiak's regional Native corporation is growing its shareholders, dividends & finances
claims.source_outlet: KMXT Kodiak Public Broadcasting, reported by Davis Hovey
claims.notes: Background. Incorporation dated nearly 55 years ago, consistent with 1971 and the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act.

claims.claim: The Koniag Education Foundation has awarded more than 10 million dollars and over 4,000 scholarships and currently supports 158 students.
claims.verbatim: More than $10 million in scholarships and grants awarded to Koniag Shareholders and their Descendants
claims.source_outlet: Koniag Education Foundation
claims.notes: The foundation's own numbers, so treat more than as the foundation's framing.

claims.claim: Koniag Government Services is named as a donor to the Koniag Education Foundation.
claims.verbatim: Koniag Government Services (KGS)
claims.source_outlet: Koniag Education Foundation
claims.notes: The loop the deck wants to show, contracting revenue returning as scholarships. Leisnoi is also listed as a donor. No dollar amount is attached to any donor, so do not imply one.

claims.claim: Immigration and Customs Enforcement awarded a task order to Koniag Services Inc with $17,456,917.40 obligated.
claims.verbatim: THE PURPOSE OF THIS TASK ORDER IS TO PROVIDE SUPPORT SERVICES IN SUPPORT OF ENFORCEMENT AND REMOVAL OPERATIONS 287G NATIONAL COORDINATION CENTER
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: PIID 70CDCR26FR0000034, signed July 28th, 2026, vendor address 3800 Centerpoint Dr Ste 700, Anchorage. Koniag Services Inc is one of the 28 KGS subsidiaries in C24. THE COUNTERWEIGHT, AND IT MUST SHIP.

claims.claim: The ICE task order took effect on August 6th, 2026 and can run to August 5th, 2030.
claims.verbatim: KONIAG SERVICES, INC.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: Period of performance August 6th, 2026 to August 5th, 2030, current completion August 5th, 2027. The four year span does NOT support calling it a one year contract.

claims.claim: The federal record now gives the place of performance for the ICE call center as Nashville and not the small town first named.
claims.verbatim: NASHVILLE, TN 372143749
claims.source_outlet: Federal Procurement Data System FPDS-NG public ATOM feed
claims.notes: IMPORTANT CORRECTION. The scout described a call center in Adams, Tennessee, a town of about 600. Adams was the site first named; ICE later moved the planned site to Nashville and the live FPDS record reflects it. If the deck mentions Adams at all it must say originally named and later moved.

claims.claim: The ICE call center contract was reported as being worth up to 63 million dollars.
claims.verbatim: Federal documents show Alaska corporation to operate ICE 24-hour call center in Tennessee
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media, reported by Anita Wadhwani of the Tennessee Lookout
claims.notes: SOFTEN. Write reportedly worth up to 63 million dollars. FPDS shows $17,456,917.40 actually obligated, so 63 million is a reported ceiling over four years and is not money spent. If the deck prints one number, print the obligated figure from C38. The reporting names Koniag Government Services while the federal record names its subsidiary Koniag Services Inc.

claims.claim: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered a line by line review of every small business sole source award above 20 million dollars.
claims.verbatim: a line-by-line review of all small business sole source and set aside awards above $20 million in contract value
claims.source_outlet: Hunton Andrews Kurth government contracts briefing
claims.notes: NON PRIMARY, MUST BE LABELLED. A law firm quoting a memorandum dated January 16th, 2026. No Pentagon document was reachable. Corroborated consistently by Alaska Public Media, KNBA, KNOM, KYUK, Federal News Network and Washington Technology. NOTHING IN THE DECK MAY IMPLY ANY CONTRACT NAMED HERE HAS ACTUALLY BEEN REVIEWED. The Leisnoi contract sits just above the threshold, which is an arithmetic fact and nothing more.

claims.claim: Commonwealth North's executive director wrote that nobody has quantified how much of Alaska Native corporation revenue runs through 8(a) contracts.
claims.verbatim: Nobody has quantified how much of that $13.5 billion runs through 8(a) contracts.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News opinion, by Ross Johnston
claims.notes: Verified verbatim on the fetched page. Johnston is executive director of Commonwealth North. The thesis line for the deck.

claims.claim: Alaska's twelve Native regional corporations reported 13.5 billion dollars in combined 2022 revenue.
claims.verbatim: $13.5 billion in combined 2022 revenue
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News opinion, by Ross Johnston
claims.notes: Corroborated by the Commonwealth North forum writeup dated May 27th, 2026. Attribute to Commonwealth North, since it is a 2022 figure quoted in 2026.

claims.claim: About 9 billion dollars of that revenue was earned outside Alaska.
claims.verbatim: about $9 billion was earned elsewhere and carried home
claims.source_outlet: Commonwealth North
claims.notes: Two fetched pages agree.

claims.claim: The regional corporations distribute 300 to 350 million dollars a year through dividends, elder benefits and scholarships.
claims.verbatim: $300 to $350 million a year, distributed through dividends, elder benefits, and scholarships
claims.source_outlet: Commonwealth North
claims.notes: Two fetched pages agree.

claims.claim: About 110,000 Alaska Native shareholders live in Alaska, roughly 15 percent of the state population.
claims.verbatim: About 110,000 shareholders live in the state, roughly 15% of the population
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News opinion, by Ross Johnston
claims.notes: PRECISION WARNING. Commonwealth North gives roughly 150,000 shareholders total, about 110,000 in Alaska. KEEP THE QUALIFIER in Alaska.

claims.claim: 8(a) contracting is roughly 4 percent of all federal contracting.
claims.verbatim: roughly 4 percent of all federal contracting
claims.source_outlet: Commonwealth North
claims.notes: Two fetched pages agree. Useful for scale, since it undercuts any framing of 8(a) as dominant.

claims.claim: Emil Notti said of 8(a) that it is not DEI and that it distributes earnings broadly.
claims.verbatim: It is not DEI. It does not create individual wealth. It is not corporate enrichment. It distributes earnings broadly.
claims.source_outlet: Commonwealth North
claims.notes: Verified word for word. Attribute as Notti told a Commonwealth North forum, since this is a host organisation's summary and not a transcript.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly put a data centre moratorium request on both its state and its federal 2027 legislative priority lists.
claims.verbatim: a request to temporarily halt the development of large commercial data centers in Alaska
claims.source_outlet: KUAC, reported by Patrick Gilchrist
claims.notes: KUAC reports only one item appears in both the state and federal parts of the list, and it is this one. Corroborated by the Fairbanks Daily News-Miner on August 30th, 2026.

claims.claim: The Assembly approved those priorities at its meeting on August 27th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly adopted an exhaustive list of 2027 state and federal legislative priorities on Thursday
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks Daily News-Miner, reported by Jack Barnwell
claims.notes: DATE RESOLVED by two source inference, not a primary reading. Two outlets say Thursday; the News-Miner published Sunday August 30th and KUAC Monday August 31st, so the only preceding Thursday is August 27th. Borough minutes were unreachable. If the deck prefers zero risk, write in late August 2026.

claims.claim: Leisnoi Inc is an Alaska Native village corporation with roots on Woody Island in the Kodiak archipelago.
claims.verbatim: an Alaska Native village corporation with roots on Woody Island in the Kodiak Island Archipelago
claims.source_outlet: Leisnoi, Inc.
claims.notes: The corporation's own description. The same page says it owns approximately 50,000 acres on Kodiak, Woody and Long Islands.

claims.claim: Leisnoi Inc lists Leisnoi Professional among its companies and the Leisnoi Professional site names Leisnoi Professional Services LLC.
claims.verbatim: Our diverse companies are focused on providing best-in-class services to clients in the federal and private arenas and delivering value back to our Alaska Native Shareholders.
claims.source_outlet: Leisnoi, Inc.
claims.notes: THE SOFTEST LINK IN THE DECK, DELIBERATELY WORDED SHORT. No page states that Leisnoi Professional Services LLC is a subsidiary of Leisnoi, Inc. The chain followed today is that the Leisnoi, Inc. companies page links Leisnoi Professional to leisnoiprofessional.com, that domain redirects to leisnoi-gs.com, and that site lists Leisnoi Professional Services, LLC among its companies. WRITE IT AS a listed company of Leisnoi Inc, NEVER as a wholly owned subsidiary, and draw no corporate family tree on a slide. Contrast C23, where Koniag states ownership outright.

claims.claim: A Bering Straits Native Corporation shareholder petition had garnered 102 signatures from shareholders and descendants, and 20 from non-shareholders, as of early December.
claims.verbatim: had garnered as of early December 102 signatures from shareholders and descendants, and 20 signatures from non-shareholders.
claims.source_outlet: The Nome Nugget, by Diana Haecker, January 8th, 2026
claims.notes: VERIFIED LATE, during the Phase 8 aggregate pass, because the scout carried the figure and the first claims pass did not. The 102 is a SNAPSHOT as of early December and includes descendants, who are not shareholders, so the slide may not write 102 shareholders. It also excludes the 20 non-shareholder signatures, so 102 is not the petition's total. Print the as-of and print and descendants, both of which slide 08 now does.

claims.claim: The petition calls on Bering Straits Native Corporation to divest from all business contracts associated in any way with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention centers immediately.
claims.verbatim: The petition calls on BSNC to divest from all business contracts associated in any way with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention centers immediately.
claims.source_outlet: The Nome Nugget, by Diana Haecker, January 8th, 2026
claims.notes: This is what the shareholders asked for, not what BSNC did. BSNC is a DIFFERENT corporation from Koniag, which is the deck's subject, and slide 08 must never let the two blur. The petition is on the page as the register in which Alaskans argue about this, and for no other reason.

killed.claim: Leisnoi Professional Services LLC is a subsidiary of Leisnoi, Inc., the ANCSA village corporation for Woody Island
killed.why: No source states the ownership relationship. usaspending lists the recipient parent name as the company itself. Downgraded to C53, which claims only that Leisnoi Inc lists Leisnoi Professional among its companies.

killed.claim: HQ003425CE092 is the largest contract found
killed.why: False. Tuknik 140D0421C0002 totals $24,210,536.43 and 140D0419C0047 totals $21,596,322.25, both larger. Do not use largest without a defensible qualifier.

killed.claim: Tuknik contract 140D0419C0047 is worth roughly $9,479,118.55 as a floor
killed.why: Wrong. That is only the first three obligating actions. All fourteen total $21,596,322.25. Replaced by C20.

killed.claim: The DOE contract ceiling was raised from $24,524,561.40 to $34,301,950.89
killed.why: The prior value appears on no fetchable page. usaspending publishes only the current ceiling and the FPDS ATOM feed carries no ceiling field. A before and after must not be printed.

killed.claim: The 30 Koniag actions span 12 named agencies
killed.why: 13 departments, or 16 at contracting office level. Replaced by C27, which writes more than a dozen.

killed.claim: The Koniag Shareholder Settlement Trust totals $46,013,900 after a $3,117,600 contribution
killed.why: Unverified and dead. No fetched page contains either figure. The 2026 annual report is behind a shareholder portal.

killed.claim: Koniag Government Services took a roughly $63 million one-year DHS contract to run an ICE call center in Adams, Tennessee, a town of about 600
killed.why: Three errors. The record names Koniag Services Inc, not KGS. The term runs August 6th, 2026 to August 5th, 2030, so not one year. $17,456,917.40 is obligated against a reported 63 million ceiling. And the live place of performance is Nashville, because ICE moved the site off Adams. Replaced by C38 through C41.

killed.claim: The Alaska Beacon and Anita Wadhwani reported the ICE call center story
killed.why: Misattributed. Wadhwani writes for the Tennessee Lookout. Both alaskabeacon.com and tennesseelookout.com return 403. The fetched source is the Alaska Public Media republication of August 12th, 2026.

killed.claim: Koniag distributed its $33 per share dividend on January 27th, 2026
killed.why: Half killed. The $33 figure survives as C33. The year does not, because the KMXT article of October 9th, 2025 gives January 27 with no year. Print the day without the year or drop it.

killed.claim: Place of performance queries can use the field name PRINCIPAL_PLACE_STATE_NAME
killed.why: Not a deck claim but recorded so a later run does not repeat it. That field silently returns zero entries for queries that do have results. The working field is POP_STATE_NAME. A second instance of the same failure mode as the central story.
